en.title: Weekly Global Macro — The limits of monetary relief: industrial divergence, energy costs and the repricing of capital
en.deck: A retrospective review of 16–22 November: US industrial output, Chinese demand and investment, European inflation, oil supply and the conditional transmission of financial-market losses to credit.
en.regime: Uneven expansion with persistent inflation and limited room for monetary relief.
en.key_risk: Asset repricing could amplify weaker demand if credit terms tighten while energy delivery costs remain high.
watch: US PCE and GDP releases scheduled for 25 November

signal_rationale.delta: Integrates the November 16–22 data releases and compares real activity, inflation, energy supply and capital repricing rather than treating Friday market prices as the entire weekly macro assessment.
signal_rationale.evidence: Fed G17 October -0.4% m/m; China industrial value added +4.8% y/y, retail consumer goods +0.4%, fixed asset investment -8.1% Jan–Oct; Eurostat HICP 4.0%, ONS CPI 3.6%; IEA oil supply 105.4 mb/d; ECB financial stability review.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Household demand, sectoral production and investment affect orders and revenue; imported energy and funding costs influence the marginal financing decision.
signal_rationale.transmission: Conditional energy delivery costs → input prices or margins → inflation and policy response → borrowing terms and investment; asset prices may affect collateral and credit but flows are not inferred.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Synchronized improvement in household demand, investment and output with easing prices and stable credit markets would weaken the thesis.

key_constraints: Review period 16–22 November 2026, information cutoff 22 November 23:59 BRT; retrospective production on 26 November, not original publication date.
US output uses November 17 vintage before annual revision.
China investment categories overlap; sectoral growth rates not contributions.
Market observations are intraday, not synchronized weekly closing data.
No unobserved portfolio flows or country-level quantitative scenarios inferred.
Coverage of Japan and Canada is qualitative; no numerical comparison from incompatible GDP or CPI series.
Independent QA, full repository validation and production deployment not yet performed.
